note: What's waiting on John, for the admin page's Waiting on you. Kept by Claude: an item added when something needs John, marked done here ('done': date) when Claude sees it's done. 'auto' items tick themselves off from the Mac mini; the rest John ticks off.

items.title: Put the draft live
items.why: Changes to the site are on the draft until you put them live. Waiting now: editing always on in the draft, AFI details for members only (live shows none till then), For kids tightened, the series page and picture width, subtitles redrawn after skipping.
items.how: Home › Updates: look at the Preview, then press Update everything.

items.title: Set up your Mac to take queued films
items.why: So the big films you queue are converted on your Mac by themselves, freeing space on the G-Drive.
items.how: On your Mac: Conversions › Set up your Mac to take queued films, press Copy, paste into Terminal, press Return. Then Queue for my Mac on each big film.

items.title: Free up space on the G-Drive
items.why: It's nearly full; downloads and conversions need room to work.
items.how: Queue the biggest films for your Mac (Library › Largest, then Queue for my Mac on each). Delete originals you're happy with (Conversions › Originals kept). Empty “Set aside” on the G-Drive when you're sure (Mac mini › The G-Drive has the Bin).

items.title: Run the newest Criterion genres bookmarklet
items.why: It brings each box set's exact films, its description, and the Eclipse sets.
items.how: Criterion: drag “Grifflix: Criterion genres” to your bookmarks bar again (replacing the old one), open Criterion's list, click it, then choose the criterion-tags.json it saves.

items.title: Choose which Secrets & Lies to keep
items.why: Two copies: “Secrets and Lies” (Criterion, 3.5 GB, 3.3 Mbps, two soundtracks, English subtitles) and “Secrets & Lies” (2.4 GB, 2.2 Mbps, no subtitles). Keep the Criterion one.
items.how: The Copies tab (at the top) shows it once the Mac mini has its update: the Criterion copy is chosen for you; press Set the others aside.

items.title: Decide on a second drive for the films
items.why: The films themselves aren't backed up; a 16 TB drive (about £220–£260) with a nightly copy covers the G-Drive failing.
items.how: Tell Claude if you buy one, and the nightly copy will be set up.

items.title: Want one list of every box set film you're missing?
items.why: Each set shows its own missing films; this would be one spreadsheet across all of them.
items.how: Tell Claude yes or no.

items.title: Should the synopses bookmarklet fetch box sets too?
items.why: So each box set gets Criterion's own text without the genres bookmarklet.
items.how: Tell Claude yes or no.

items.title: Empty the old Grifflix Bin?
items.why: It's taking space on the G-Drive.
items.how: Tell Claude yes or no.

items.title: Use Criterion's country on the media server too?
items.why: Where Criterion and the media server disagree about a film's country.
items.how: Tell Claude yes or no.

items.title: Is Plex still used? If not, quit it on the Mac mini
items.why: It runs beside the media server on a Mac with only 4 GB of memory, and looks through the same drive.
items.how: Tell Claude. If it isn’t used, Claude asks to quit it and keep it off, and you press Allow here: no Screen Sharing.

items.title: More memory for the Mac mini (about £20–£30)
items.why: It has 4 GB and is short of it: macOS is squashing and swapping memory all day, which slows everything.
items.how: Two 4 GB DDR3 1066 MHz SO-DIMM sticks (8 GB) for a Mac mini Mid 2010: the base unscrews by hand. Or tell Claude and it'll help.
items.answer: Not doing: the new Mac mini replaces it.

items.title: Decide whether to replace the Mac mini
items.why: It's a 2010 model: USB 2 only (the G-Drive runs at a fraction of its speed), a 2-core processor flat out, and macOS too old for current tools.
items.how: A used Mac mini from 2018 or later (about £200–£350) with the same drive on USB 3. Tell Claude before buying, to check the model.
items.answer: An M6 Mac mini, arriving 27 Nov 2026.

items.title: Run both Criterion bookmarklets again, for the special features
items.why: Criterion's special features lists, for each film and each box set, ticked where you have that extra.
items.how: Criterion: drag both bookmarks to your bar again (replacing the old ones). Genres: open Criterion's list, click it, choose criterion-tags.json. Synopses: Copy your list, open criterion.com, click it, paste, then choose criterion-synopses.json (it reads every film again once, about 3 seconds each, and carries on if Criterion pauses it).

items.title: Run the AFI bookmark again, for the 55 films whose AFI pages weren’t read
items.why: 55 films have their AFI page linked but no details: 14 never read, and 41 where AFI’s search page was kept instead of the film’s. (It was 434: your runs on 22 Nov read the rest.) Not urgent.
items.how: Your bookmark is up to date if you dragged it to your bar on or after 22 Nov: it asks the Mac mini for the list when you click it. Run it on catalog.afi.com: it reads those 55 first, then looks for the films with no AFI link yet (most aren’t American, so it takes a while). Then choose the grifflix-afi.json it saves.

items.title: Re-read the genres of films Criterion only lists inside a box set?
items.why: Those films were given their whole box set's genres (as Agnès de ci de là Varda had Comedy and Musical). Re-reading them from TMDB gives them their own, but changes the genres of every such film.
items.how: Tell Claude yes or no.

items.title: Should 12A animation count as For kids?
items.why: For kids now leaves out animation rated 12A and over: The Boy and the Heron and Ne Zha 2 dropped out with By Brakhage.
items.how: Tell Claude if 12A should count; otherwise nothing to do.
items.answer: Only the rating decides: a family or animated film is For kids if rated U, PG, G or the like (26 Nov 2026).

items.title: Agnès de ci de là Varda: keep its English title?
items.why: Given its IMDb number, the media server named it Agnès Varda: From Here to There, TMDB's English title.
items.how: Tell Claude if you'd rather it kept the French title; otherwise nothing to do.

items.title: Turn picture subtitles into text?
items.why: 84 films have English picture subtitles (Blu-ray PGS or DVD) saved beside them, exactly timed, and more come with every conversion. Read into text they’d play everywhere, better than any made by Whisper.
items.how: Claude has a plan ready (in the chat, 26 Nov): tell Claude to go ahead and it’ll be built, running on your Mac like the Whisper job.

items.title: Remove the AFI text from the site's past versions on GitHub?
items.why: The AFI details are now for members only and no longer in the site's files, but copies published before stay in the repository's history.
items.how: You said yes (26 Nov). Claude needs one more yes, after reading what it can and can’t remove (in the chat): GitHub keeps copies for every pull request, which only GitHub Support can clear.

items.title: Put Argos Translate on your Mac (once, optional)
items.why: Your Mac now translates a film's own subtitles in another language (built in or beside it), or ones made for its copy, and compares them with the English before Whisper listens. It installs Argos Translate by itself the first time it needs it: a large download (around 1 GB with what it needs), which holds that first film up while it downloads.
items.how: On your own Mac, the one whose helper does Whisper's work (not the Mac mini): open Terminal, paste  ~/Grifflix/fw/bin/python3 -m pip install argostranslate "spacy<3.8"  and press Return (the quotes matter). Each language's translation model (about 100 MB) comes the first time a film in that language needs it.

items.title: Move Grifflix onto the new Mac mini
items.why: The M6 Mac mini arrives on 27 Nov. Grifflix (the media server, the gateway, the converter, the downloads) moves onto it, and the G-Drive goes on USB 3 at full speed.
items.how: Tell Claude when it’s unpacked and signed in: Claude will give you the steps, a few at a time, and do the rest itself.
